incidents.victim: Poland energy grid & European critical infrastructure
incidents.vector: Sabotage of energy and water-treatment systems plus intrusions into government networks, largely by compromising routers and edge devices left on default or weak credentials and old Cisco flaws (CVE-2018-0171, Smart Install).
incidents.impact: The UK and EU imposed their first joint cyber sanctions on 24+ Russian individuals and entities, formally blaming FSB Center 16 for a December 2025 attack that nearly blacked out heating for 500,000 Poles; a 13-nation advisory warned of ongoing critical-infrastructure targeting across defense, energy, finance, government and health sectors.

incidents.victim: Salesforce customers across retail, education & manufacturing
incidents.vector: Abuse of trusted OAuth relationships — vishing to trick staff into authorizing a malicious app posing as Salesforce Data Loader, plus supply-chain compromise of integrations (Salesloft Drift, Gainsight, Klue) and misconfigured guest/Aura access.
incidents.impact: Microsoft reported large-scale enumeration and mass exfiltration of CRM records (accounts, contacts, case data) across many tenants, with persistent API access that evaded conventional sign-in detections; not a Salesforce vulnerability but abuse of legitimate trust.

incidents.vector: A modular Go-based backdoor (~20 C2 commands) that bundles three destructive payloads — a raw disk wiper, fake ransomware with discarded keys, and a multipass secure wiper — using RabbitMQ/Redis for C2.
incidents.impact: Microsoft (which tracks it as GigaWiper) and Google (BlueRabbit) documented destructive wiper activity dating to October 2025; Binary Defense attributes the tooling to an Iran-based actor. The 'wiper inside a backdoor' lets attackers optionally destroy systems after full reconnaissance and control.

incidents.vector: A no-logs VPN service (1VPNS) and a separate 'cryptor' seller provided ransomware crews with tools to hide identities, cloak malware and evade detection; the service was taken down by the FBI and European agencies in May.
incidents.impact: The U.S. Treasury sanctioned First VPN and its Ukrainian administrator plus a Belarusian cryptor seller, saying the service abetted ransomware attacks that caused billions in losses to U.S. critical-infrastructure providers.

incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-service using edge-device exploits (Fortinet, Erlang/OTP, SMB), stolen credentials, a custom Go backdoor, an EDR-killer framework and self-propagation across ESXi/virtual infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 named The Gentlemen the second most active RaaS of 2026, with victims up roughly 6x half-over-half and a record 117 claimed in June alone; a 90% affiliate payout is fueling rapid recruitment. Manufacturing (103 of 580 victims) is the top-hit sector.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed her email account and used it to briefly hijack several Telegram channels, then published claimed private correspondence.
incidents.impact: The Black Mirror group claims to have stolen 350 GB of Sobchak's data spanning 2015–2026 and is offering the archive for sale; Sobchak says the leaked screenshots were fabricated. Authenticity could not be independently verified.

incidents.victim: Organizations behind compromised Ruckus/ASUS edge routers
incidents.vector: Exploitation of known (n-day) vulnerabilities in unpatched Ruckus and ASUS routers to deploy new custom backdoors (LONGLEASH, DOGLEASH, JARLEASH) and build Operational Relay Box proxy networks.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos assesses the China-nexus actor is expanding covert ORB infrastructure that other Chinese APTs use to mask origins and attack high-value targets, creating a resilient, hard-to-dismantle blind spot for defenders.

incidents.victim: Consumers and SMBs in the U.S. and EU
incidents.vector: Malvertising to fake 'cracked software' pages delivering a Factory-v3 Go loader (signed with a fabricated JustWatch certificate, padded with null bytes to evade sandboxes) that drops Vidar Stealer and the XMRig miner.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 tracked a mid-to-late-April 2026 campaign of 43+ loader samples stealing browser credentials, cookies and crypto wallets and mining Monero, with an in-memory AMSI bypass to disable Windows script scanning.

incidents.victim: Nissan North America, AdaptHealth and other victims
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day in a broad hacking spree hitting multiple organizations' cloud-based HR/enterprise platforms.
incidents.impact: Nissan NA and medical-equipment maker AdaptHealth (which notified the SEC) disclosed breaches tied to the spree; AdaptHealth said patient data and internal documents were accessed. No group has claimed responsibility.

incidents.victim: ~2 million home IoT devices (NetNut / Popa botnet)
incidents.vector: Residential-proxy SDKs bundled into smart-TV and streaming-box apps quietly enrolled home devices as always-on proxy exit nodes rented to cybercriminals for scraping, ad fraud and account takeover.
incidents.impact: The FBI, IRS-CI, Google and Lumen seized hundreds of NetNut domains, degrading the network (operated by Israel's Alarum Technologies) by millions of devices; Google observed 316 threat-actor clusters using NetNut exit nodes in one June week. Alarum's stock fell ~67%.

incidents.vector: A phishing-as-a-service platform abusing Microsoft's OAuth device-code flow and vendor-impersonation invoice lures to capture tokens and Primary Refresh Tokens, bypassing MFA and surviving password resets.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos detailed the ARToken panel (80+ API endpoints for token theft, BEC, and SharePoint/OneDrive exfiltration) after an incident-response engagement, showing full mailbox access and evidence-suppression inbox rules for compromised M365 accounts.

incidents.vector: A contractor published ~844 MB of internal CISA data — including AWS GovCloud admin keys and a CSV of plaintext usernames/passwords for dozens of internal systems — in a public GitHub repo for nearly six months.
incidents.impact: CISA's postmortem said it ignored nine automated alerts before external notification and took over 48 hours to rotate keys; it says logs show the credentials were not used outside its environment and no mission data was exposed.

incidents.vector: Data breach at the Japanese branch of the life-insurance company (details of intrusion not disclosed).
incidents.impact: More than 4.38 million customers were impacted; the company also disclosed a separate breach in June of the prior year.

incidents.vector: The World Leaks data-extortion group breached the Indian electronics manufacturer and leaked ~200,000 documents after it refused to pay a ransom.
incidents.impact: The leaked cache exposed images and component details of the unreleased iPhone 18 (battery, chips, circuit boards), a significant intellectual-property and supply-chain exposure for Apple.

incidents.vector: The Qilin ransomware group breached the central bank's network (traced to an incident about three weeks earlier) and leaked stolen files on the dark web.
incidents.impact: Libyan authorities are investigating the compromise of the national central bank after files allegedly taken from its network were published, raising sovereign financial-security concerns.

incidents.vector: A Ukrainian hacktivist group breached the network and executed a destructive attack, wiping systems and deleting backups.
incidents.impact: The group claims to have wiped 3,000 servers/workstations and 700 virtual machines, deleted all backups and stolen more than 650 TB of documents; the May breach was disclosed only recently.

incidents.vector: A newly emerged ransomware group compromised the company, forcing it to take its entire IT network offline.
incidents.impact: The BlackField group demanded a $2 million ransom; Nidec (formerly Nippon Densan) had also been hit by ransomware in late 2024.

incidents.victim: Jaguar Land Rover (2025 hack, newly attributed)
incidents.vector: Intrusion using novel ransomware with a previously unseen encryption algorithm; originally claimed by a group calling itself Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters.
incidents.impact: A New York Times report attributes last year's JLR hack — which halted production September to mid-October 2025 and cost the UK economy an estimated £1.9B ($2.55B), the country's costliest breach — to Russian hackers, though state direction is disputed.

incidents.vector: Intruders breached the Homeland Security Information Network — used to share sensitive data with federal, state, local and industry partners — targeting HSIN servers and a connected SharePoint system.
incidents.impact: The intrusion occurred between late May and early June; details of the intruders and what was taken remain unknown, raising concern given the network's sensitive law-enforcement information-sharing role.

incidents.vector: The ShinyHunters group breached the U.S. insurance-standards body at the start of June and maintained access to sensitive supervisory data.
incidents.impact: NAIC suspended risk designations for insurers and several credit-rating agencies paused data sharing to avoid exposure; NAIC says it has since evicted the hackers and is restoring operations.
